question.prompt: One of the factors of \(x^4+4\) is:

solutions.explanation:
The square \((x^2+2)^2\) contains \(x^4+4\), but it also has the middle term \(4x^2\). Adding and subtracting that term reveals a difference of squares:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^4+4
&=x^4+4x^2+4-4x^2\\
&=(x^2+2)^2-(2x)^2\\
&=(x^2-2x+2)(x^2+2x+2).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last step uses \(A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)\). This polynomial identity shows that \(x^2-2x+2\) is a factor, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Create a difference of squares
